American economist Stephen Roach, who previously proposed the "Hong Kong is finished" theory, has recently written another article saying the "old Hong Kong has indeed ended," questioning that Hong Kong's economic performance is overly dependent on the mainland and that the national security law and other factors have weakened Hong Kong's rule of law and freedoms. Acting Financial Secretary Wong Wai-lun today published an article in a newspaper, refuting Roach's remarks without naming him, stating that recently "some media commentaries have attempted to paint a bleak picture of Hong Kong's prospects," and that Hong Kong must correct the misinformation spread by "naysayers."

Wong Wai-lun wrote an article today to refute criticisms that painted a bleak picture of Hong Kong's prospects, pointing out that in the first half of this year, Hong Kong's IPO fundraising was double that of the same period last year. He attended the listing ceremony of mainland optical module manufacturer InnoLight Technology this morning, describing it as "the largest IPO project in Hong Kong's capital market in nearly seven years." (Photo: Wong Wai-lun's Facebook)

Wong Wai-lun today published an article in Sing Tao Daily, titled "Hong Kong: Embracing a New Era of Opportunities," pointing out that recent media commentaries have attempted to paint a bleak picture of Hong Kong's prospects, ignoring Hong Kong's resilience and vitality, and turning a blind eye to enormous opportunities. He stated that Hong Kong must refute these criticisms with concrete actions, "correcting the misinformation spread by those naysayers."

He then cited various data, pointing out that Hong Kong's economy has undergone a "strong rebound," including the economy contracting by 3.7% when the current government took office in 2022, then growing by 3.6% last year, while the 5.9% growth in the first quarter of this year marked the largest increase in five years. He noted that foreign trade has been rising, with exports continuing to grow, while in June this year, merchandise exports and imports increased by 53.4% and 45.4% year-on-year respectively. In the first half of this year, Hong Kong had 87 IPOs (initial public offerings), with fundraising reaching HK$210.2 billion, nearly double that of the same period last year; as of the end of June, over 500 applications were still being processed.

Citing the 2026 Global Wealth Report, Wong Wai-lun noted that Hong Kong has become the world's largest cross-border wealth management centre; last year, Hong Kong-registered authorised funds recorded net inflows of HK$357 billion, while the number of family offices increased by over 25% compared to two years ago. Hong Kong also continues to hold the title of the world's freest economy, with its global competitiveness ranking rising to second place.

He concluded by stating that "some critics seem to be driven more by prejudice against China" rather than objective analysis, and that the criticisms are unsupported by evidence and inconsistent with facts. He reiterated that investors and talent are full of confidence in Hong Kong.
